story.title: FlyDubai Co-Pilot Attacked Captain with Axe, Barred from Flying Over Extremism Concerns
story.summary: The co-pilot of a FlyDubai flight to Israel, identified as Omani national Hamam al-Hammami, attacked the captain with an axe in what UAE officials describe as an attempted terrorist act. Al-Hammami had previously been barred from flying in Oman due to concerns over extremist views. The incident has raised alarms within the aviation industry, already struggling from recent crises.

explore_lenses.label: Who is investigating, and under what law?
explore_lenses.title: The UAE says it has legal jurisdiction
explore_lenses.summary: Although the aircraft landed in Saudi Arabia, UAE authorities say they have jurisdiction because the aircraft is UAE-registered. Prosecutors describe the case as an attempted terrorist act but say the inquiry is unfinished.

claims.text: The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs said UAE judicial authorities have jurisdiction because the aircraft is registered in the UAE and flies under its flag; it says UAE law applies to crimes aboard it even outside UAE territory.

UAE Prosecutor General Hamad Saif al-Shamsi said investigators concluded the co-pilot began carrying out a terrorist plan by attacking the captain with a crash axe and attempting to take the controls.
The prosecutor's office says it is still examining motives, possible connections, and physical, digital, and technical evidence before announcing final results.

explore_lenses.label: How did prior concerns not stop him flying?
explore_lenses.title: Hiring and screening are central questions
explore_lenses.summary: Reporting based on unnamed officials says the co-pilot had previously been removed from flying duties in Oman over extremism concerns before Flydubai hired him. The available record does not yet establish what information was shared or reviewed during hiring.

claims.text: Associated Press, citing a regional official and a person familiar with the case, reported that Oman barred the co-pilot from flying over concerns about extremist views and moved him to an administrative Oman Air job before he was hired by Flydubai.

A Gulf diplomat told AP that the co-pilot underwent standard security checks before hiring, but that those checks appeared focused on criminal convictions rather than a deeper review for possible radicalization.
Flydubai says a full official investigation is under way and asks that the process establish the facts; it has not publicly detailed its hiring or vetting procedures in this case.
AP reported that Oman Air and Oman's government had not publicly commented on the reported prior restrictions as of October 3, 2026.

story_report.summary: UAE authorities say Flydubai co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami attacked the captain of a flight bound for Israel with an axe and attempted to take the controls, an act prosecutors describe as the beginning of a terrorist plan. The alleged attack has prompted an official investigation, with UAE authorities asserting jurisdiction over the UAE-registered aircraft. Investigators are examining evidence and possible connections, but officials have not publicly established a motive, whether anyone directed the act, or whether the suspect had organizational links.

sections.heading: UAE Prosecutors’ Investigation and Jurisdiction
sections.body: The prosecutor’s office says it is reviewing physical, digital and technical evidence, along with possible motives and connections, before announcing final results. UAE Prosecutor General Hamad Saif al-Shamsi said investigators concluded that the attack and alleged attempt to seize the controls began the execution of a terrorist plan. The foreign ministry says UAE law applies to crimes aboard the aircraft because it is registered in the UAE and flies under its flag, including when outside UAE territory.

sections.heading: Flydubai Hiring and Oman Restrictions
sections.body: Associated Press, citing a regional official and a person familiar with the case, reported that Oman barred al-Hammami from flying over concerns about extremist views and transferred him to an administrative Oman Air role before Flydubai hired him. A Gulf diplomat told AP that pre-employment checks appeared to focus on criminal convictions rather than a deeper review for possible radicalization. Flydubai says a full official investigation is under way and has not publicly detailed its hiring or vetting procedures in the case.

unresolved.text: Authorities have not publicly established the alleged attacker’s motive, whether anyone directed the act, or whether he had links to an organization.
It is not publicly confirmed what Flydubai knew about the reported Omani restrictions, what records were available during hiring, or whether any screening failure occurred.
